On the account-history surfaces — /users/me/security-history, /users/me/free-tier-status, and the notification inbox (GET /notifications, GET /notifications/summary), whose bodies carry security, billing and infrastructure events — absent/false is a hard 403, because a history has no meaningful reduced view.

deny_reauthorization.description: Opt-in least-privilege belt for scoped/script tokens. When true, the server strips the `resources.create_tokens` and `resources.vault` permission leaves from the resolved token, forces `vault_access` to false, and forces a bounded (non-permanent) expiry — producing a locked-down leaf that can never re-delegate or reach the vault. Rejected (400) if combined with an explicit `create_tokens`/`resources.vault`/`vault_access` grant. Defaults to false; omitted callers are unaffected.

get.description: Retrieve the profile of the currently authenticated user. Works with JWT, auth token, or Basic authentication. When authenticated with an auth token, response includes `data.auth_token` introspection details (permissions and realm restrictions). This endpoint works even for banned users (read-only access). Note: when authenticated with an auth token that lacks the `resources.read_account` permission, the response is reduced to identity fields (id, username, alias, public_key, timestamps); email and other account PII are omitted.

signup_method.description: How the user signed up (email, github, google, admin)

free_tier_unlocked_at.description: When the account was unlocked for free-tier claiming.

public_key.description: Optional ED25519 public key (64 hex characters)

public_storage.description: Optional public JSON profile storage (max 64KB serialized)

ip_whitelist.description: Array of whitelisted IP addresses/CIDR ranges or "*" for all IPs

realm_ids.description: List of realm IDs this token is restricted to. Empty means no specific realm restrictions (unless allow_no_realm is false).

allow_no_realm.description: Whether this token can be used without a realm scope (e.g. on base domain). Set to false for strict sub-account tokens.

permissions.title: TokenPermissions
permissions.description: Fine-grained permissions for this token. Any missing permission path defaults to false (deny).

kvm.description: Can enable /dev/kvm passthrough (run full VMs inside a container). Rented/dedicated servers only.

delete.description: Can delete projects

auth_token_public_profile.description: Can update the current auth token public_key and public_storage via self endpoint

create_tokens.description: Can mint/copy/manage child auth tokens within its own subtree (delegated token issuance). Children are clamped to a subset of this token; default-deny.

read_account.description: Can read the owning account's PII. On the profile endpoints (/auth/me, GET/PUT /users/:id self) absent/false DEGRADES the response to identity fields (id, username, alias, public_key, timestamps). On the account-history surfaces — /users/me/security-history, /users/me/free-tier-status, and the notification inbox (GET /notifications, GET /notifications/summary), whose bodies carry security, billing and infrastructure events — absent/false is a hard 403, because a history has no meaningful reduced view.

event_access.description: Whether this token can access real-time event streams and event history endpoints

delegation_depth.description: Delegation chain depth. 0 = root (account-minted); child = creator depth + 1.

post.summary: Issue a fresh audience-bound identity claim
post.description: Mint a fresh, audience-bound identity claim for the authenticated caller without a re-login. First-party JWT sessions only — auth tokens, HTTP Basic, and impersonated sessions are rejected. The claim proves "Hoody authenticated this user" to the audience named in the request; third parties verify it offline against GET /api/v1/meta/public-key. Claim lifetime is clamped to [60s, min(server ceiling — default 24h, remaining JWT lifetime)], default 1 hour.

identity_claim.title: IdentityClaim
identity_claim.description: Hoody-signed identity credential for third-party verification. Verify with: nacl.sign.detached.verify(UTF8(payload_b64), hexToBytes(signature_hex), hoodyPublicKey) Fetch Hoody's public key at: GET /api/v1/meta/public-key Re-issued claims are audience-bound: verifiers MUST check payload.aud against their own identifier.

kid.description: Key ID — look up the matching key in GET /api/v1/meta/public-key keys[]

payload_b64.description: base64url-encoded JSON payload containing: claim_type ("identity"), iss ("hoody-api"), sub (user_id), username, type ("user"|"admin"), iat, exp, kid, aud (audience binding)

signature_hex.description: ED25519 detached signature over UTF-8 bytes of payload_b64 (128 hex chars = 64 bytes)

expires_in.description: Effective lifetime in seconds after clamping

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 expiry timestamp

audience.description: The audience the claim is bound to
Consumer identifier this claim is bound to (e.g. your app hostname). Verifiers reject the claim unless they expect exactly this audience. Printable ASCII, no whitespace or double quotes.

expires_in.description: Requested claim lifetime in seconds. Clamped to [60, min(server ceiling, remaining JWT lifetime)]. Default: server-configured (1h).

get.description: Returns your own account security history — sign-ins and, on request, rejected attempts and other security events (logout, 2FA changes, OTP outcomes) — with IP address, resolved country, source channel and timestamp, newest first. **History covers the last 180 days, which is platform policy and the same for every account; older logins are purged automatically and cannot be recovered.** Login records cannot be edited or deleted by the account holder — the trail is append-only so it stays trustworthy as evidence. Pass `include_failed=true` to also see REJECTED sign-in attempts — a burst of them, or any from a country you have not visited, is the clearest sign someone else is trying to get in. Failures are only recorded when a credential was presented against a REAL account (an attempt on an unknown address is never recorded, so this cannot be used to test whether an account exists), and are capped at 200 per account per hour — beyond that, further attempts in the same hour are not listed. Pass `include_security=true` for other account-security events: logout, 2FA enable/disable, OTP verification outcomes and backup-code use. `country` is resolved in the background after the event is recorded. It is `null` when the address is not geolocatable at all (private, reserved, or IPv6 — these stay null permanently), when the provider returned no country for it, or when resolution has not completed. Treat null as **unavailable**, never as a location — and note that a null does not necessarily become non-null later: background retries stop once the row ages out of the retry window.

name.description: Name for the container. Must be 3-100 characters, alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores. Omit or use "rand" to generate a random name.

color.description: HEX color for the container (e.g., #FF0000 or FF0000). If not provided, a random color will be generated. The # prefix will be added automatically if missing, and the color will be converted to uppercase.

container_image.description: Container image to use. If null or not provided, will use the default configured image. Shorthand is resolved automatically: a bare distribution name or a hyphenated version ("debian", "debian-13") becomes the canonical base image ("debian/13"), as do the "debian:13" and "debian 13" forms.

ai.description: Whether AI features are enabled (default: true)

ssh_public_key.description: SSH public key for container access. SSH public keys must be unique per container (one container per key). If not provided, will inherit from project defaults.

comment.description: Optional comment for the container (max 16000 characters)

hoody_kit.description: Enable all Hoody Kit features (extra-apt-sources, apt-proxy, basic-packages, dev-packages, extra-shells, hoody-daemon, sudo-env, remove-snapd, webview, desktop, user, ttyd, vm-packages). vm-packages is the hoody-vm QEMU runtime (~185 MiB); running VMs additionally needs the separate kvm grant.

dev_kit.description: Enable dev_kit development tools in the container. Defaults to true when hoody_kit is true, false when hoody_kit is false (unless explicitly set). Cannot be updated after creation.

kvm.description: Enable /dev/kvm passthrough (run full VMs inside the container) at creation. Available on rented / dedicated (bare-metal) servers ONLY — never free tier — and rejected (403) on a free server. Defaults to false. Can also be toggled later via PUT /containers/{id}/kvm on a stopped container.

dev_kvm.description: Accepted alias of `kvm` on input (`kvm` wins if both are sent and they must agree).

autostart.description: Whether the container should start automatically on host boot (default: true)

ramdisk.description: Whether to mount a ramdisk at /ramdisk in the container (default: true). The ramdisk KEEPS data when you stop/start/reboot the container, but LOSES data if the physical host server reboots. Can store up to 50% of total host memory. Ideal for security (data automatically wiped on server seizure), temporary files, or extremely fast I/O at no cost.

cache.description: Enable use of cached images during container creation (--use-cache-image). When false, no cache options are added.

cache_image.description: Force the creation of a new cached image from the container image. This option is only available to admins or the owner of the image.

prespawn.description: INTERNAL — not user-settable. Prespawn cache containers are provisioned only by the system pool producer. Passing `true` is rejected (403); an explicit `false` is accepted.

bypass_prespawn.description: Bypass prespawn container claiming and create a fresh container directly. By default (false), the system will attempt to claim a matching prespawn container if available.

realm_ids.description: Realm IDs to assign this container to. get.description: Get all containers across all projects for the current user with pagination, filtering, and sorting. This endpoint provides a global view of all containers without being scoped to a specific project.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination - starts from 1

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of containers to return per page - maximum 100 items

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Field to sort containers by

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort direction - ascending or descending

parameters.name: realm_id
parameters.description: Filter by realm ID. Only returns containers that belong to this realm. Alternative to using realm subdomain in URL.

parameters.name: runtime
parameters.description: Include live runtime information. Accepts "true", "false", or a URL-encoded JSON string like `{"displays":true}`. An empty JSON object `{}` fetches all info. Results are cached for 2 seconds to prevent abuse.

parameters.name: include_proxy_domains
parameters.description: Include proxy domains (aliases) for each container. When true, adds a proxy_domains array to each container object.

parameters.name: include_proxy_permissions
parameters.description: Include the full proxy-permissions documents (container-level proxy_permissions and parent-project-level project_proxy_permissions) for each container. Returns proxy authentication group configuration including credentials — request only when explicitly needed. Auth tokens additionally require the resources.proxy_aliases permission.

parameters.name: include_prespawn
parameters.description: Include prespawn containers in the listing. By default, prespawn containers are excluded from results.

parameters.name: include_expired
parameters.description: Include containers that have expired due to server termination. By default, expired containers are excluded from results.

parameters.name: include_deleting
parameters.description: Include containers currently being deleted. By default, deleting containers are excluded from results.

has_proxy_permissions.description: True when a non-default proxy-permissions configuration is stored for this container or its project (auth groups, program rules, default-deny policy, proxy disabled, or hooks). post.description:
Issues a signed, portable container authorization claim.

The returned `container_claim` is an ED25519-signed credential that proves:
- Who the user is (sub, type)
- Which container they are authorized for (containerId, projectId)
- When Hoody issued the authorization (iat, exp)

Container programs can verify this claim **offline** using Hoody's public key
at `GET /api/v1/meta/public-key` — no API round-trip needed during verification.

Claims expire after `HOODY_CONTAINER_CLAIM_EXPIRES_IN` (default 6h). Clients
should re-call this endpoint to refresh before expiry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Container ID (24-char hex)

X-Hoody-Signature.description: ED25519 signature of response body. Format: t=<unix_ts>,kid=<keyId>,path=<urlPath>,sig=<128-hex>

container_claim.description: The signed container authorization claim bundle.

kid.description: Key ID used to sign this claim. Look up this key from GET /api/v1/meta/public-key.

payload_b64.description: base64url-encoded JSON payload of the container claim.

signature_hex.description: ED25519 signature as 128 lowercase hex characters.

container_id.description: The authorized container ID (echo of path:id).

ramdisk.description: Ramdisk (tmpfs) facts for this container. This is MEMORY, not disk — it counts against your memory allowance on that server — which is why it sits beside `memory` and contributes to no disk total. Present only when the container has a ramdisk and the server reports a pool for it.

scope.description: Sharing scope. `container` = private scopes only. `project` = additionally a /ramdisk/project shared with your other containers in this project ON THE SAME SERVER. A RAM disk is memory on one server, so it cannot span servers: containers of the same project placed on different servers each get their own project scope, not a shared one.

shared_pool_maximum.description: Server-wide tmpfs ceiling in bytes. SHARED and UNRESERVED: your other containers on the same server draw from it, so this is NOT a quota for this container and must not be used as the denominator of a usage percentage. Null when the server does not report a ceiling.

capacity_reserved.description: Whether any of `shared_pool_maximum` is held for this container. Always false: the pool is first-come, first-served. Renderers should read this before considering a progress bar.

usage.title: ContainerRamdiskScopeUsage
usage.description: Measured bytes per scope, or null when this response did not measure. The container LIST endpoint never measures (it would cost one host round trip per container per poll), so it always reports null here — meaning "open the container to measure", NOT "empty".

private.description: Bytes in this container's own /ramdisk. Null means the host could not measure it; 0 means measured and empty. These are different facts.

secrets.description: Bytes in this container's /ramdisk/secrets. Null = unmeasurable, 0 = measured empty.

project.description: Bytes in the SHARED /ramdisk/project. Present only for scope `project`. Shared with sibling containers, so adding it to `private` double-counts across them.

get.summary: Unread notification count and newest position
get.description: Lightweight polling endpoint: returns the unread count and the newest notification position without any notification bodies. Use this to detect new notifications; fetch the list only when something changed. Auth-token callers must hold the `resources.read_account` permission; tokens without it receive 403. It is gated with the list rather than left open because the count and the newest timestamp are an activity oracle for the notifications themselves. JWT/owner callers are unaffected.

is_capped.description: True when unread_count hit unread_cap and is a floor, not an exact total.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Server-advertised poll cadence. Clients MUST honour this rather than hardcoding an interval.

get.summary: List notifications for the authenticated user
get.description: Paginated list of the notifications visible to the authenticated user (global notifications plus those targeted to them), newest first. Results are PAGINATED — page 1 is not the complete set; follow pagination.next_cursor (or increment page) to read the rest. Notification bodies carry account-security, billing and infrastructure events, so auth-token callers must hold the `resources.read_account` permission; tokens without it receive 403. JWT/owner callers are unaffected.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (offset paging). Ignored when `before` is supplied.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page (max 100).

parameters.name: unread_only
parameters.description: Return only notifications the user has not read. Mutually exclusive with read_only.

parameters.name: read_only
parameters.description: Return only notifications the user HAS read — the archive half of the inbox. `pagination.total` counts the same filtered set, so it can drive page numbers directly. Mutually exclusive with unread_only (sending both is a 400, not an empty page).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Keyset cursor from a previous response's pagination.next_cursor ("<created_at>,<id>"). Prefer this over `page` for an inbox: offset paging duplicates or skips rows when a new notification arrives mid-read.

patch.description: Enable or disable the proxy for a project. Disabling is a kill-switch, not a bypass: while enable_proxy is false, new requests that reach the proxy permission layer are denied with 403, evaluated before authentication groups, permission rules and the default policy, so no configured rule can re-open access while it is off. Containers keep running; only proxy reachability is cut. Note the project value applies only to containers that do not set enable_proxy themselves - a container document with enable_proxy true overrides a disabled project, and saving a container permissions document persists an explicit true. Use the container-level endpoint to disable a specific container reliably.

container_id.description: Container ID that this alias points to. You must own this container.

alias.description: Custom alias name (a-z, 0-9, hyphens only, 3-61 chars, cannot start/end with hyphen) OR null/false for auto-generated 48-char hex. Must be unique across every container hosted on the same physical server, including containers owned by other tenants — not merely within your own account. Reserved and rejected: the exact label "containers" (an infrastructure label of the container proxy domain), and anything equal to "egress"/"workspaces" or starting with "egress-"/"workspaces-". Distinct labels such as "containers-my-app" and "proxymyapp" are allowed.

program.description: Which container service the alias targets — a built-in Hoody program ("terminal", "files", "code", "browser", "agent", "display", …) or a transport protocol ("http", "https", "ssh"). To point an alias at an HTTP server you run yourself inside the container (a process started via the daemon, a dev server, anything listening on a TCP port) use program "http" — or "https" for a TLS backend — and give the port via the "port" field (e.g. program "http" + port 3000 forwards to http://<container>:3000). The combined "http-3000" form and the legacy "index"-as-port form also work; when more than one is supplied the order of authority is port > the port embedded in "http-<port>" > index, so a leftover/default index can never override a real port. Must be a name or alias from container-programs.json.

port.description: Target port for the "http"/"https" protocol — the port your server listens on inside the container (e.g. program "http" + port 3000 → http://<container>:3000). Preferred, unambiguous way to point an alias at a raw HTTP/HTTPS server; takes precedence over "index" and over any port embedded in the program string ("http-3000"). Ignored for built-in Hoody programs, which have fixed kit ports.

index.description: Instance index, or (legacy) target port for the "http"/"https" protocol. Defaults to 1. For a built-in Hoody program it selects which running instance to route to (e.g. terminal 2). For "http"/"https" it is the port your server listens on inside the container — but prefer the dedicated "port" field; if "port" or a port embedded in the program ("http-3000") is also supplied, that wins over this index (so an accidental index of 1 will not route you to port 1).

target_path.description: Base path for routing. Requests to https://{alias}.../ will be forwarded to the container with this path prefix. Auto-prefixed with / if missing.

allow_path_override.description: Whether to allow paths beyond target_path. If false, only the exact target_path is accessible.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO 8601 expiration date. Alias will be automatically disabled after this date.

enabled.description: Whether the alias is initially enabled (defaults to true)

source_path.description:
ARCHITECTURE NOTE: Source containers control WHAT to share (this path), NOT WHERE it appears in targets. Target mount paths are determined automatically by the server infrastructure - users cannot specify arbitrary mount locations in target containers.

SECURITY-HARDENED: Absolute path in source container. Character whitelist (a-z A-Z 0-9 / - _.), path normalization applied, blocks system paths (/proc/*, /sys/*, /dev/*, /boot/*, /run/*, /var/run/*), no path traversal (..), no null bytes. Returns normalized canonical path.

Examples of ALLOWED paths:
 ✅ /home/user/data - User home directories
 ✅ /opt/application/files - Application software
 ✅ /var/lib/app/shared - Application state data
 ✅ /data/team-files - Custom data paths

Examples of BLOCKED paths:
 ❌ /proc/* - Kernel interfaces, process memory
 ❌ /sys/* - Hardware interfaces, kernel parameters
 ❌ /dev/* - Device files, raw disk/memory access
 ❌ /boot/* - Boot files, kernel images
 ❌ /run/* - Runtime secrets, sockets
 ❌../etc - Path traversal attempts
 ❌ /proc/../etc - Bypass attempts via normalization

source_path.description:
ARCHITECTURE NOTE: Source containers control WHAT to share (this path), NOT WHERE it appears in targets. Target mount paths are determined automatically by the server infrastructure - users cannot specify arbitrary mount locations in target containers.

SECURITY-HARDENED: Absolute path in source container. Character whitelist (a-z A-Z 0-9 / - _.), path normalization applied, blocks system paths (/proc/*, /sys/*, /dev/*, /boot/*, /run/*, /var/run/*), no path traversal (..), no null bytes. Returns normalized canonical path.

Examples of ALLOWED paths:
 ✅ /home/user/data - User home directories
 ✅ /opt/application/files - Application software
 ✅ /var/lib/app/shared - Application state data
 ✅ /data/team-files - Custom data paths

Examples of BLOCKED paths:
 ❌ /proc/* - Kernel interfaces, process memory
 ❌ /sys/* - Hardware interfaces, kernel parameters
 ❌ /dev/* - Device files, raw disk/memory access
 ❌ /boot/* - Boot files, kernel images
 ❌ /run/* - Runtime secrets, sockets
 ❌../etc - Path traversal attempts
 ❌ /proc/../etc - Bypass attempts via normalization

get.summary: Get Hoody API Signing Public Key
get.description:
Returns the ED25519 public key(s) used by Hoody to sign all API responses
(X-Hoody-Signature header), identity claims issued at login, and container
authorization claims.

**Third-party verification flow:**
1. Fetch this endpoint once (cache for 24h+)
2. Locate the key by `kid` from the `keys[]` array
3. For response signatures: parse `X-Hoody-Signature: t=<ts>,kid=<id>,m=<method>,s=<status>,path=<url>,sig=<hex>`
 and verify sig against the newline-joined tuple `${t}\n${method}\n${status}\n${path}\n${responseBody}`
4. For identity/container claims: verify `claim.signature_hex` against `claim.payload_b64` bytes
5. If `kid` in a signature/claim does not match any cached key, re-fetch this endpoint.

No authentication required. This endpoint is intentionally public.

X-Hoody-Signature.description: ED25519 signature of the response. Format: t=<unix_ts>,kid=<keyId>,m=<method>,s=<status>,path=<urlPath>,sig=<128-hex>; signed data is the newline-joined t/method/status/path/body tuple

keys.description: JWKS-style array of active signing keys. Currently one key; supports multiple during rotation.

kid.description: Key identifier. Incremented on rotation (v1 → v2). Look up by kid when verifying.

public_key_hex.description: 32-byte ED25519 public key as 64 lowercase hex characters.

public_key_b64url.description: Same key as base64url (URL-safe, no padding).

active_kid.description: The kid of the currently active signing key. New signatures will use this key.

get.description:
Returns cached counters for the public Hoody social channels: GitHub stars,
Telegram members, Discord members (total + currently online), X followers,
and LinkedIn followers.

Values are persisted to disk and refreshed in the background
(default every 10 minutes), so the endpoint is cheap, has no upstream
rate-limit risk, and survives process restarts even when upstreams are
unreachable.

A field is `null` only when no value has ever been persisted for it (e.g.
first boot before the first successful refresh). Once populated it stays
populated until manually cleared.

No authentication required.

github.description: GitHub repository star count. Null if the GitHub source is not configured or has never returned a successful response.

telegram.description: Telegram channel/group member count. Null if not configured.

discord.description: Approximate Discord guild member count. Null if not configured.

discord_online.description: Approximate Discord members currently online. Null if not configured.

x.description: X (Twitter) follower count for the configured handle. Scraped from public profile HTML — may be null if X changes its markup; the previous good value is kept on failure.

linkedin.description: LinkedIn company-page follower count. Scraped from public HTML — may be null if LinkedIn changes its markup; the previous good value is kept on failure.

fetchedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last refresh that successfully updated at least one source. Null until the first successful refresh.

post.description: Rent an available server for a specified duration. Some servers carry a ONE-TIME setup fee charged only on this first payment (never on extension); when they do, the request must confirm the total via max_charge_cents.

setup_fee_cents.description: FROZEN one-time setup fee charged when this rental started, in integer cents. 0 when none applied. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

total_paid_cents.description: amount_cents + setup_fee_cents. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

renewal_pricing_frozen.description: The renewal tiers this rental is guaranteed, frozen at purchase: a map of days to integer cents. A CEILING, not a fixed price — a later price CUT is passed on, a rise is not. Null for a rental that predates the freeze, where the current server tiers apply. Omitted for tokens without financial.billing.read.

x-error-codes.title: Wallet balance too low
x-error-codes.description: The wallet balance is below the total required for this rental. The response `data` breaks the total down into rental_cents, setup_fee_cents, required_cents and available_cents so a client can explain the shortfall — a customer quoted the tier price alone would otherwise see an unexplained failure when a one-time setup fee applies.
x-error-codes.resolution: Top up the wallet to at least required_cents, then retry.

x-error-codes.title: Rental duration not offered
x-error-codes.description: rental_days must match a duration the server actually prices. There is no interpolation: 5 days is unrentable unless a "5" tier exists.
x-error-codes.resolution: Pick one of pricing.available_durations and retry.

x-error-codes.title: Server has no pricing configured
x-error-codes.description: The server has no pricing row, or none covering the requested duration.
x-error-codes.resolution: Choose a different server, or contact support to have pricing configured for it.

x-error-codes.title: Server not available for rental
x-error-codes.description: The server is not rentable: it is already rented, not ready, or not offered for rental. Also returned when a concurrent request won the race for it.
x-error-codes.resolution: Re-read GET /api/v1/servers/available and pick a currently available server.

x-error-codes.title: One-time setup fee must be confirmed
x-error-codes.description: This machine carries a one-time setup fee, charged once when the rental starts and never on an extension. The request omitted max_charge_cents, so the total was never confirmed and nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: The exact figures are in this error's data: show the customer data.setup_fee_cents as a one-time charge and data.total_cents as what they will pay now, then retry with max_charge_cents set to data.total_cents. Do not compute the total yourself.

example.message: This machine has a one-time setup fee. Please confirm the total before proceeding.

x-error-codes.title: The total must be confirmed before money moves
x-error-codes.description: The request would debit an account and carried no max_charge_cents, so there was nothing to bind the quoted price to the charged one. Nothing was charged. This applies to every paid purchase, including servers with no one-time setup fee — the fee is a separate thing, and its absence never meant the total did not need confirming.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the current total, show it to the customer, and retry with max_charge_cents set to the value they confirmed. Never auto-retry with the total from this error: that defeats the confirmation it exists to obtain.

example.message: Please confirm the total before proceeding.

x-error-codes.title: Price changed since the quote
x-error-codes.description: The live total (rental price plus any one-time setup fee) is higher than the max_charge_cents ceiling supplied with the request, so nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Re-read the listing — GET /api/v1/servers/available for an in-stock server (the total is pricing.price_tiers[rental_days].total_first_payment), or GET /api/v1/offers for an offer — show the user the new total, and retry with an updated max_charge_cents once they confirm. Do NOT auto-retry with the returned actual value — that would defeat the confirmation.

example.message: The price changed — please review the current total and confirm again.

x-error-codes.title: Stored pricing is misconfigured
x-error-codes.description: The server's stored pricing did not pass validation when the charge was attempted. The request fails closed and nothing is charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: This server cannot be rented until its pricing is corrected — please contact support. Retrying beforehand cannot succeed.

example.message: Server pricing is misconfigured and cannot be charged. Please contact support.

rental_days.description: Number of days to rent (must match server pricing durations, max 3650)

max_charge_cents.description: Ceiling on the TOTAL debit (rental price + one-time setup fee), in integer cents. REQUIRED for every paid rental. Omitting it returns 409 CHARGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, or 409 SETUP_FEE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED when the server also carries a one-time fee. It is NOT optional for fee-less servers: the fee is a separate charge, and its absence never meant the total did not need confirming. Only a total of zero needs no ceiling. If the live total exceeds this ceiling the request is rejected with 409 CHARGE_EXCEEDS_MAX and nothing is charged; re-read the server and confirm the new total. A ceiling (not an exact match) so a price DROP still succeeds. Read it from pricing.price_tiers[rental_days].total_first_payment.

is_free_tier.description: True for synthesized free-tier subserver entries (no ServerRental row backs them; rental_end is a non-expiring sentinel).

container_capacity.description: Occupied container slots vs this server's effective limit ("X / Y containers"). Present ONLY for free-tier servers currently held by the caller, on genuine first-party JWT sessions — absent for dedicated/bare-metal servers (no limit applies), for auth-token, HTTP Basic, impersonated, or realm-scoped requests (not disclosed), and for past rentals. `used` counts capacity slots with the exact semantics the SERVER_CONTAINER_LIMIT error enforces: in-flight (creating/copying/claiming) and prespawn rows occupy a slot; failed/deleted/deleting rows do not — so it can differ from the number of containers you see listed. `max` may be 0 when new container creation is paused on this server. A create that claims a matching prespawn on the same server is count-neutral and can still succeed at used == max. The pair corresponds to the error envelope's current_count/limit.

expected_rental_end.description: The rental's CURRENT rental_end, exactly as the API returned it. The extension is applied only if it still matches, so a retried request — a lost response, a double click — is refused with 409 EXTENSION_ALREADY_APPLIED instead of charging and extending a second time. Re-read the rental before retrying; never resend blindly.

additional_days.description: Number of additional days to extend the rental (must match server pricing durations, max 3650)

max_charge_cents.description: The total you confirmed, in whole cents. The extension is refused if it would cost more. REQUIRED when the rental has no frozen renewal price (409 CHARGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED) — without a quoted ceiling nothing bounds what the current server tiers can charge. Optional when the rental still carries frozen tiers, which are themselves a ceiling the customer accepted at purchase.

x-error-codes.description: This machine carries a one-time setup fee, charged once when the rental starts and never on an extension. The request omitted max_charge_cents, so the total was never confirmed and nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: The exact figures are in this error's data: show the customer data.setup_fee_cents as a one-time charge and data.total_cents as what they will pay now, then retry with max_charge_cents set to data.total_cents. Do not compute the total yourself.

x-error-codes.title: The total must be confirmed before money moves
x-error-codes.description: The request would debit an account and carried no max_charge_cents, so there was nothing to bind the quoted price to the charged one. Nothing was charged. This applies to every paid purchase, including servers with no one-time setup fee — the fee is a separate thing, and its absence never meant the total did not need confirming.
x-error-codes.resolution: Read the current total, show it to the customer, and retry with max_charge_cents set to the value they confirmed. Never auto-retry with the total from this error: that defeats the confirmation it exists to obtain.

example.message: Please confirm the total before proceeding.

x-error-codes.title: Price changed since the quote
x-error-codes.description: The live total (rental price plus any one-time setup fee) is higher than the max_charge_cents ceiling supplied with the request, so nothing was charged.
x-error-codes.resolution: Re-read the listing — GET /api/v1/servers/available for an in-stock server (the total is pricing.price_tiers[rental_days].total_first_payment), or GET /api/v1/offers for an offer — show the user the new total, and retry with an updated max_charge_cents once they confirm. Do NOT auto-retry with the returned actual value — that would defeat the confirmation.

get.description:
Creates a new browser instance or returns metadata for an existing one.
This is the primary endpoint for explicitly creating browser instances.

**Key capabilities**:
- Create isolated browser instances with custom configurations
- Retrieve metadata for existing instances
- Configure browser emulation (user agent, viewport, geolocation)
- Set locale and timezone for accurate geolocation

**Instance identification**: Each instance is uniquely identified by its `browser_id`. Multiple instances can run concurrently with different IDs.

The response includes the `webSocketDebuggerUrl` field which provides the Chrome DevTools
WebSocket endpoint for remote debugging (when available with `useRemoteDebuggingPort: true`).

parameters.name: browser_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the browser instance (0-based index)

parameters.name: chromiumVersion
parameters.description:
Chromium/Chrome version selection for the instance.
This option applies only when `browser=chromium`.

Supported formats:
- Full version: `136.0.7103.113`
- Major version: `136` (mapped to a known stable patch for the current OS)
- Channel tag: `stable`, `beta`, `dev`, `canary`

The server will **block** until the required browser is downloaded into `BROWSERS_DIR`.

parameters.name: fingerprintId
parameters.description:
Base fingerprint profile id.
The server will load `storage/config/fingerprints/<fingerprintId>.json` and use its `context` and `launch`
defaults, then apply any request overrides.

parameters.name: useRemoteDebuggingPort
parameters.description:
If `true`, the child process will launch Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port` and will populate
`webSocketDebuggerUrl` in metadata responses.

parameters.name: remoteDebuggingPort
parameters.description: Optional fixed DevTools port (only used when `useRemoteDebuggingPort=true`). If omitted, a free port is chosen.

parameters.name: remoteDebuggingAddress
parameters.description: Interface address for DevTools. Defaults to `127.0.0.1`. Use `0.0.0.0` only in trusted environments.

Comma-separated list (or JSON array string) of absolute extension directory paths to load.
Extensions require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode) and will launch a persistent profile.

Directory containing extension subfolders to load (each subfolder is treated as an extension).
Extensions require `showBrowser=true` (headful mode) and will launch a persistent profile.

parameters.name: extensionsStoreIds
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list (or JSON array string) of Chrome Web Store extension IDs to download and load.
Requires `showBrowser=true` and works only with `browser=chromium`.

parameters.name: proxyServer
parameters.description:
Proxy server for browser traffic. Supports `http://`, `https://`, `socks5://`, or `socks5h://`.
Example: `socks5://127.0.0.1:9050`

Example: {"latitude":40.7128,"longitude":-74.0060,"accuracy":100}

parameters.description:
Launch Chromium in stealth mode using Patchright (anti-detection patches).
Only applies to `browser=chromium`. Ignored for Firefox.

parameters.description:
Enable or disable the full-page display iframe on the root URL.
When enabled (default), navigating to `/` serves an HTML page with an iframe pointing to the Hoody display URL.

parameters.description:
Control the `maximize_new_windows` flag stamped onto generated display URLs (iframe pages, status pages, `iframe_url` metadata). The flag is always explicit (`true` or `false`); when true the hoody-display client opens new top-level app windows maximized.
Enabled by default; set to `false` to keep the display client's centered default-size placement (the explicit `false` also overrides a display-side `default-settings.txt` enable).
Explicit `iframe_url` values are never modified.

get.description:
Navigates to a URL and/or captures a screenshot of a browser tab.

**Navigation + Screenshot workflow**:
- If `url` is provided: Navigate to URL → Wait for page load → Capture screenshot
- If `url` is omitted: Capture screenshot of current page state

**Key features**:
- Smart tab management with `onlyIfNotExists` to avoid duplicate tabs
- Multiple output formats: PNG, JPEG, or Base64-encoded
- Full page capture with `fullPage=true`
- Quality control for JPEG compression

**Common use cases**: Visual regression testing, website monitoring, content verification

get.description:
Returns the Chrome DevTools WebSocket URL and HTTP discovery URL for the specified
browser instance. The HTTP URL (`/json/version`) can be used to resolve the WebSocket
endpoint automatically.

**Hoody CDP relay**: In container deployments these URLs are minted on the `cdp-{N}`
hostname (e.g. `https://{projectId}-{containerId}-cdp-{N}.{server}.containers.hoody.com`),
paired 1:1 with the `browser-{N}` instance that owns the debugging session. The relay is
reached HTTP-first: connect with `chromium.connectOverCDP("https://…-cdp-{N}/")`, which
fetches `/json/version` to resolve the live WebSocket endpoint before upgrading, and
cold-starts instance `N` on demand if it isn't already running. Only the read-only
discovery endpoints (`/json/version`, `/json/list`, `/json`) and DevTools WebSocket
sessions (`/devtools/browser/<id>`, `/devtools/page/<id>`) are relayed — mutation endpoints
(`/json/new`, `/json/close`, `/json/activate`) are not exposed.

**Availability**: These URLs are populated when the instance is launched with
`useRemoteDebuggingPort=true` and `browser=chromium`. Otherwise it will be `null`.

A declared `default: true` is therefore not a description of the server's behaviour, and any client that materialises schema defaults into the request sends the operator-override on every call — the Hoody CLI did exactly that until 2026-08-10. get.description:
Read-only: returns the instance's current viewport policy without mutating anything.
`viewport: null` means fixed-viewport emulation is disabled (responsive — the page follows the real window size).
`source` is `creation` until the first successful `POST /viewport`, then `runtime`.
`converged` reports whether every live page currently reflects the policy.

**Never auto-creates an instance.** `browser_host`/`browser_port` may be omitted when exactly one instance is running (it is selected); with zero instances the response is 404, with more than one it is 400 `AMBIGUOUS_INSTANCE`.

parameters.name: browser_host
parameters.description: Instance host. Optional — must be paired with browser_port; when both are omitted the single running instance is selected (400 AMBIGUOUS_INSTANCE with more than one).

parameters.name: browser_port
parameters.description: Instance port. Optional — must be paired with browser_host.

400.description: Ambiguous instance (host/port omitted with multiple instances running) or invalid parameters

502.description: The instance's control process did not answer (parent proxy failure)

post.description:
Mutates the running instance's viewport policy. JSON body only:
- Fixed size: `{"viewport": {"width": 1280, "height": 800}}` (integers 1..8192; no other keys)
- Responsive (follow the real window): `{"viewport": null}`

Applies to every currently-open tab; tabs opened later inherit the policy.

**Constraints**:
- Responsive requires a Chromium instance that was CREATED responsive (`noViewport=true`/`viewport=null` on /start). Instances created with a fixed viewport respond `409 REQUIRES_RESTART` (close and recreate the instance responsive instead).
- Firefox: fixed sizes work; responsive responds `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`.
- Partial application failures respond `502 VIEWPORT_APPLY_INCOMPLETE` with `details.failedTabs`.

**Never auto-creates an instance.** Instance selection rules are identical to `GET /viewport`.

parameters.name: browser_host
parameters.description: Instance host. Optional — must be paired with browser_port; when both are omitted the single running instance is selected (400 AMBIGUOUS_INSTANCE with more than one).

parameters.name: browser_port
parameters.description: Instance port. Optional — must be paired with browser_host.

200.description: Viewport policy applied to all live tabs

409.description: REQUIRES_RESTART — instance was created with a fixed viewport; responsive requires recreating it

501.description: NOT_SUPPORTED — responsive at runtime is Chromium-only

502.description: VIEWPORT_APPLY_INCOMPLETE — some tabs failed to apply (details.failedTabs)

viewport.description: Fixed size {width,height} (integers 1..8192, no other keys), or null for responsive.

get.description:
Returns the main VS Code web interface.

## Authentication
- If authentication is enabled and user is not logged in, redirects to `/login`
- Session is managed via cookies

## Workspace Handling
- If no `folder` or `workspace` parameter: uses last opened or CLI argument
- Stores query parameters in settings for next session
- Supports both folder and workspace (.code-workspace) files

## Extension-Only Mode
Add `?extension=PUBLISHER.NAME` to open in extension-only mode:
- Hides file explorer
- Focuses on extension's UI
- Ideal for embedding extensions as standalone apps (like Cline)

## Custom Resources
Use `--external-js` and `--external-css` flags to inject external resources:
- JavaScript files are loaded in <head>
- CSS files are linked as stylesheets
- CSP headers are automatically updated to allow external domains

## Page Loader
Enable `--page-loader` to show a branded loading overlay during initialization.
The loader automatically dismisses when VS Code is ready.

get.description:
Proxies requests to applications running on local ports.

## URL Structure
`/proxy/:port/*` where:
- `:port` - Local port number (1024-65535)
- `*` - Path to proxy (e.g., /api/data)

## Behavior
- Strips `/proxy/:port` from the path before forwarding
- So `/proxy/3000/api/data` → `http://localhost:3000/api/data`
- Supports all HTTP methods
- Supports WebSocket upgrade
- Requires authentication (unless --skip-auth-preflight for OPTIONS)

## Example
If you have an app on port 3000:
- Direct: `http://localhost:3000/api/users`
- Proxied: `https://code.example.com/proxy/3000/api/users`

get.description:
Proxies requests to local ports with path passthrough.

## Difference from /proxy/:port/*
- `/proxy/:port/*` - Strips the prefix before forwarding
- `/absproxy/:port/*` - Keeps the full path including `/absproxy/:port/`

## When to use
Use when the proxied app needs to be aware it's running under a subpath.
The app must be configured to serve from `/absproxy/:port/`.

## Configuration
Set `--abs-proxy-base-path` to customize the base path.

post.description:
Execute an HTTP request using libcurl with comprehensive configuration options. Supports both synchronous (immediate response) and asynchronous (background job) execution modes. Includes advanced features like retry logic, cookie sessions, proxy configuration, and automatic response storage.

**Execution Modes:**
- `sync` (default): Blocks until completion, returns immediate response
- `async`: Returns job ID immediately, executes in background

**Response Modes:**
- `transparent` (default): Returns raw response with original headers
- `json`: Wraps response in JSON with timing metrics and metadata

**Example Use Cases:**
- API integration with automatic retry
- Large file downloads with progress tracking
- Multi-step authentication flows with session cookies
- Scheduled recurring requests with cron expressions

post.description:
Create a new cron-based schedule that executes an HTTP request repeatedly at specified intervals. Schedules are persistent and survive server restarts.

**Cron Expression Format:** 6 fields - `second minute hour day month weekday`
- `0 * * * * *` - Every minute
- `0 0 * * * *` - Every hour

parameters.name: notification_server_url
parameters.description:
External notification server URL for real-time notification integration.

**URL Format:**
`https://{project}-{container}-n-{display}.{node}.containers.hoody.com/notification-client.js`

**Auto-detection:**
If not provided, the client will attempt to auto-detect from the current hostname pattern.
The client transforms the display URL pattern by replacing 'display' with 'n'.

**Examples:**
- Manual: `?notification_server_url=https://my-project-container-n-6.node.containers.hoody.com/notification-client.js`
- Auto-detected from: `https://my-project-container-display-6.node.containers.hoody.com`

**Integration:**
The notification server (port 3999) provides:
- Historical notification retrieval
- Real-time WebSocket notification updates
- Notification icons serving
- Desktop notification triggering

See external notification server OpenAPI spec for complete API documentation.

schema.description: azureblob backend configuration

access_tier.description:
Access tier of blob: hot, cool, cold or archive.

Archived blobs can be restored by setting access tier to hot, cool or
cold. Leave blank if you intend to use default access tier, which is
set at account level

If there is no "access tier" specified, Hoody doesn't apply any tier.
Hoody performs "Set Tier" operation on blobs while uploading, if objects
are not modified, specifying "access tier" to new one will have no effect.
If blobs are in "archive tier" at remote, trying to perform data transfer
operations from remote will not be allowed. User should first restore by
tiering blob to "Hot", "Cool" or "Cold".

account.description:
Azure Storage Account Name.

Set this to the Azure Storage Account Name in use.

Leave blank to use SAS URL or Emulator, otherwise it needs to be set.

If this is blank and if env_auth is set it will be read from the
environment variable `AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` if possible.

archive_tier_delete.description:
Delete archive tier blobs before overwriting.

Archive tier blobs cannot be updated. So without this flag, if you
attempt to update an archive tier blob, then Hoody will produce the
error:

 can't update archive tier blob without --azureblob-archive-tier-delete

With this flag set then before Hoody attempts to overwrite an archive
tier blob, it will delete the existing blob before uploading its
replacement. This has the potential for data loss if the upload fails
(unlike updating a normal blob) and also may cost more since deleting
archive tier blobs early may be chargable.

chunk_size.description:
Upload chunk size.

Note that this is stored in memory and there may be up to
"--transfers" * "--azureblob-upload-concurrency" chunks stored at once
in memory.

client_certificate_password.description:
Password for the certificate file (optional).

Optionally set this if using
- Service principal with certificate

And the certificate has a password.

client_certificate_path.description:
Path to a PEM or PKCS12 certificate file including the private key.

Set this if using
- Service principal with certificate

client_id.description:
The ID of the client in use.

Set this if using
- Service principal with client secret
- Service principal with certificate
- User with username and password

client_secret.description:
One of the service principal's client secrets

Set this if using
- Service principal with client secret

client_send_certificate_chain.description:
Send the certificate chain when using certificate auth.

Specifies whether an authentication request will include an x5c header
to support subject name / issuer based authentication. When set to
true, authentication requests include the x5c header.

Optionally set this if using
- Service principal with certificate

delete_snapshots.description: Set to specify how to deal with snapshots on blob deletion.

directory_markers.description:
Upload an empty object with a trailing slash when a new directory is created

Empty folders are unsupported for bucket based remotes, this option
creates an empty object ending with "/", to persist the folder.

This object also has the metadata "hdi_isfolder = true" to conform to
the Microsoft standard.

disable_checksum.description:
Don't store MD5 checksum with object metadata.

Normally Hoody will calculate the MD5 checksum of the input before
uploading it so it can add it to metadata on the object. This is great
for data integrity checking but can cause long delays for large files
to start uploading.

disable_instance_discovery.description:
Skip requesting Microsoft Entra instance metadata

This should be set true only by applications authenticating in
disconnected clouds, or private clouds such as Azure Stack.

It determines whether Hoody requests Microsoft Entra instance
metadata from `https://login.microsoft.com/` before
authenticating.

Setting this to true will skip this request, making you responsible
for ensuring the configured authority is valid and trustworthy.

encoding.description:
The encoding for the backend.

See the [encoding section in the overview](/overview/#encoding) for more info.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint for the service.

Leave blank normally.

env_auth.description:
Read credentials from runtime (environment variables, CLI or MSI).

See the [authentication docs](/azureblob#authentication) for full info.

key.description:
Storage Account Shared Key.

Leave blank to use SAS URL or Emulator.

list_chunk.description:
Size of blob list.

This sets the number of blobs requested in each listing chunk. Default
is the maximum, 5000. "List blobs" requests are permitted 2 minutes
per megabyte to complete. If an operation is taking longer than 2
minutes per megabyte on average, it will time out (
[source](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/setting-timeouts-for-blob-service-operations#exceptions-to-default-timeout-interval)
). This can be used to limit the number of blobs items to return, to
avoid the time out.

memory_pool_flush_time.description: How often internal memory buffer pools will be flushed. (no longer used) (in seconds)

memory_pool_use_mmap.description: Whether to use mmap buffers in internal memory pool. (no longer used)

msi_client_id.description:
Object ID of the user-assigned MSI to use, if any.

Leave blank if msi_object_id or msi_mi_res_id specified.

msi_mi_res_id.description:
Azure resource ID of the user-assigned MSI to use, if any.

Leave blank if msi_client_id or msi_object_id specified.

msi_object_id.description:
Object ID of the user-assigned MSI to use, if any.

Leave blank if msi_client_id or msi_mi_res_id specified.

no_check_container.description:
If set, don't attempt to check the container exists or create it.

This can be useful when trying to minimise the number of transactions
Hoody does if you know the container exists already.

no_head_object.description: If set, do not do HEAD before GET when getting objects.

password.description:
The user's password

Set this if using
- User with username and password

public_access.description: Public access level of a container: blob or container.

sas_url.description:
SAS URL for container level access only.

Leave blank if using account/key or Emulator.

service_principal_file.description:
Path to file containing credentials for use with a service principal.

Leave blank normally. Needed only if you want to use a service principal instead of interactive login.

 $ az ad sp create-for-rbac --name "<name>" \
 --role "Storage Blob Data Owner" \
 --scopes "/subscriptions/<subscription>/resourceGroups/<resource-group>/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/<storage-account>/blobServices/default/containers/<container>" \
 > azure-principal.json

upload_concurrency.description:
Concurrency for multipart uploads.

This is the number of chunks of the same file that are uploaded
concurrently.

If you are uploading small numbers of large files over high-speed
links and these uploads do not fully utilize your bandwidth, then
increasing this may help to speed up the transfers.

In tests, upload speed increases almost linearly with upload

post.description: Backblaze B2

mount_paths.description: Filesystem paths where this backend is mounted (empty for newly connected backends)

schema.description: b2 backend configuration

account.description: Account ID or Application Key ID.

chunk_size.description:
Upload chunk size.

When uploading large files, chunk the file into this size.

Must fit in memory. These chunks are buffered in memory and there
might a maximum of "--transfers" chunks in progress at once.

5,000,000 Bytes is the minimum size.

copy_cutoff.description:
Cutoff for switching to multipart copy.

Any files larger than this that need to be server-side copied will be
copied in chunks of this size.

The minimum is 0 and the maximum is 4.6 GiB.

disable_checksum.description:
Disable checksums for large (> upload cutoff) files.

Normally Hoody will calculate the SHA1 checksum of the input before
uploading it so it can add it to metadata on the object. This is great
for data integrity checking but can cause long delays for large files
to start uploading.

download_auth_duration.description:
Time before the public link authorization token will expire in s or suffix ms|s|m|h|d.

This is used in combination with "Hoody link" for making files
accessible to the public and sets the duration before the download
authorization token will expire.

The minimum value is 1 second. The maximum value is one week.

download_url.description:
Custom endpoint for downloads.

This is usually set to a Cloudflare CDN URL as Backblaze offers
free egress for data downloaded through the Cloudflare network.
Hoody-VFS works with private buckets by sending an "Authorization" header.
If the custom endpoint rewrites the requests for authentication,
e.g., in Cloudflare Workers, this header needs to be handled properly.
Leave blank if you want to use the endpoint provided by Backblaze.

The URL provided here SHOULD have the protocol and SHOULD NOT have
a trailing slash or specify the /file/bucket subpath as Hoody will
request files with "{download_url}/file/{bucket_name}/{path}".

Example:
> https://mysubdomain.mydomain.tld
(No trailing "/", "file" or "bucket")

encoding.description:
The encoding for the backend.

See the [encoding section in the overview](/overview/#encoding) for more info.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint for the service.

Leave blank normally.

hard_delete.description: Permanently delete files on remote removal, otherwise hide files.

lifecycle.description:
Set the number of days deleted files should be kept when creating a bucket.

On bucket creation, this parameter is used to create a lifecycle rule
for the entire bucket.

If lifecycle is 0 (the default) it does not create a lifecycle rule so
the default B2 behaviour applies. This is to create versions of files
on delete and overwrite and to keep them indefinitely.

If lifecycle is >0 then it creates a single rule setting the number of
days before a file that is deleted or overwritten is deleted
permanently. This is known as daysFromHidingToDeleting in the b2 docs.

The minimum value for this parameter is 1 day.

You can also enable hard_delete in the config also which will mean
deletions won't cause versions but overwrites will still cause
versions to be made.

See: [Hoody backend lifecycle](#lifecycle) for setting lifecycles after bucket creation.

memory_pool_flush_time.description: How often internal memory buffer pools will be flushed. (no longer used) (in seconds)

memory_pool_use_mmap.description: Whether to use mmap buffers in internal memory pool. (no longer used)

test_mode.description:
A flag string for X-Bz-Test-Mode header for debugging.

This is for debugging purposes only. Setting it to one of the strings
below will cause b2 to return specific errors:

 * "fail_some_uploads"
 * "expire_some_account_authorization_tokens"
 * "force_cap_exceeded"

These will be set in the "X-Bz-Test-Mode" header which is documented
in the [b2 integrations checklist](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integration-checklist).

upload_concurrency.description:
Concurrency for multipart uploads.

This is the number of chunks of the same file that are uploaded
concurrently.

Note that chunks are stored in memory and there may be up to
"--transfers" * "--b2-upload-concurrency" chunks stored at once
in memory.

upload_cutoff.description:
Cutoff for switching to chunked upload.

Files above this size will be uploaded in chunks of "--b2-chunk-size".

This value should be set no larger than 4.657 GiB (== 5 GB).

version_at.description:
Show file versions as they were at the specified time.

Note that when using this no file write operations are permitted,
so you can't upload files or delete them.

versions.description:
Include old versions in directory listings.

Note that when using this no file write operations are permitted,
so you can't upload files or delete them.

impersonate.description:
Impersonate this user ID when using a service account.

Setting this flag allows Hoody, when using a JWT service account, to
act on behalf of another user by setting the as-user header.

The user ID is the Box identifier for a user. User IDs can found for
any user via the GET /users endpoint, which is only available to
admins, or by calling the GET /users/me endpoint with an authenticated
user session.

See: https://developer.box.com/guides/authentication/jwt/as-user/

owned_by.description: Only show items owned by the login (email address) passed in.

root_folder_id.description: Fill in for Hoody to use a non root folder as its starting point.
